title: Vertical Stretch of a Parabola
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Give an equation for the graph of y = x^2 - 1 after it is stretched vertically by a factor of 3.

steps.title: Recall the Vertical Stretch Rule
steps.explanation: To stretch the graph of y = f(x) vertically by a factor of c > 1, multiply the entire right-hand side f(x) by c.
steps.why: Multiplying every output by c scales the vertical distance of every point from the x-axis by a factor of c.

steps.title: Apply the Vertical Stretch Factor c = 3
steps.why: Setting c = 3 stretches the graph vertically away from the x-axis by a factor of 3.

steps.title: Distribute to Obtain Standard Form
steps.explanation: Distributing 3 across x^2 - 1 yields y = 3x^2 - 3, whose vertex is stretched from (0, -1) to (0, -3) while its x-intercepts remain at (+/-1, 0).
steps.why: Vertical scaling leaves x-intercepts (where y = 0) fixed and multiplies the y-intercept by 3.
